data.title: Upravnik Platform
data.excerpt: Property-management platform for residential buildings in Serbia. Residents, building managers, and board members each get their own view of the same building, including its money.
data.excerpt_xl:
Upravnik Platform is a role-based property-management system for residential buildings in Serbia. It replaces the WhatsApp group, the paper notice in the lobby, and the spreadsheet nobody else can see with one place for announcements, forum threads, private support tickets, chat, and the building's finances.

I built all of it in one Nx monorepo: a NestJS/Prisma/PostgreSQL API and a Next.js/React frontend. The data model, the access rules, the finance ledger, and every screen are mine.

building.title: One building, modelled strictly.
building.lede: Residential buildings in Serbia mostly run informally: a notice pinned in the lobby, a WhatsApp group for complaints, the money in a spreadsheet only the manager sees. The housing law still gives every owner the right to see the building's account, and obliges the upravnik to keep records and report on them.
body: Accounts are never self-registered. The upravnik creates each resident's account and hands over the generated credentials, which matches how it already works: the manager knows who lives in which apartment. A public sign-up would mean verifying that claim; this way there is nothing to verify.

engineer.title: The engineer's seat.
engineer.body: Underneath the three seats, every request asks one question: who is this, and which building are they in? The rest of the page is how that question gets answered, how the money stays honest, and what isn't built yet.

architecture.title: One monorepo, two apps.
architecture.intro: An Nx workspace holding apps/backend and apps/frontend. Both repositories were merged in with their history in September 2026, and CI runs lint, test, and build on whatever a change affects.

apps.name: Backend
apps.body: NestJS and Prisma over PostgreSQL in Docker, with JWT auth, a Socket.IO gateway for building chat, and generated API docs. The validation pipe rejects any field an endpoint didn't declare, environment variables are checked at boot, and files go to S3-compatible storage.

apps.name: Frontend
apps.body: Next.js App Router with a route group per role. TanStack Query is the only server-state layer, with one API module and one hook module per backend resource. Amounts never become floats: they arrive as strings and the arithmetic runs in integer paras with BigInt.

layers.models: BuildingMember: one role per user per building

layers.name: Interaction

layers.name: Finance
layers.models: 15 models: ledger, invoices, fee rules, charges, statement imports, budgets, files

access.title: Denied unless declared.
access.lede: Every HTTP handler declares exactly one access policy. The app refuses to boot if a handler has none, or if a building-scoped route is missing the parameter the guard reads.

policies.name: @InBuilding(...roles)
policies.note: A member of this building, with one of these roles.

policies.name: @InComplex(...roles)
policies.note: The caller's highest active role across the complex's buildings.

body: One AccessService turns a user plus a building into a role, and both the HTTP routes and the WebSocket chat go through it. Rules a role can't express, like a resident seeing only their own tickets or nobody replying to a closed thread, are plain functions in one file.
The user is reloaded on every request, so a disabled account, or a token issued before a password change, gets 401.

matrix.caption: Every filled cell is an assertion in the e2e suite, run against a real PostgreSQL database. A dash means that pair isn't asserted.

growth.title: How it got here
growth.body: Authorization first grew in three layers, an admin guard, a roles guard, and inline checks in services, attached controller by controller. An audit found real holes: an upravnik could reset the password of a member of another building (S1), a ticket could be opened in a building the caller didn't belong to (S2), generated passwords used Math.random (S4), and the JWT secret had a hard-coded fallback (S5). Rather than patch endpoints one by one, I inverted the default, and every finding got a regression test.

money.title: Money that can't be quietly edited.
money.lede: Finance went in on 5 October 2026 as phases 1–4 of a written plan, grounded in the housing law: owners may see the account, the upravnik must keep records and report, and fees split per unit and per square metre.

ledger.caption: Illustrative data
ledger.lock: Report for September published. Period locked.

points.title: An immutable ledger
points.body: Transactions are never edited or deleted. A correction is a storno entry linked to the original, and a unique key means a transaction can be reversed once. Invoices are cancelled with a reason, and their paid status is derived, never stored.

points.title: Decimals end to end
points.body: Decimal(14,2) in PostgreSQL, serialized as strings and summed in SQL. The frontend works in integer paras with BigInt and accepts amounts the way people type them in Serbia: 12.500,50.

points.title: Charges, exactly once
points.body: Fee rules per unit or per square metre generate monthly charges. A cron job runs at 06:00 on the 1st, Belgrade time, and a Postgres advisory lock per building means the scheduler and a manual click can't charge twice.

points.title: Bank statement import
points.body: CSV statements in UTF-8 or windows-1250 are deduplicated by a hash of the line plus its occurrence count, so two identical payments on one day stay two payments. Lines are matched to units by poziv na broj and to suppliers by account number, reviewed, then committed all-or-nothing.

points.title: Reports lock the period
points.body: A server-rendered PDF report, once published, locks its period. Any write dated inside it returns 409, checked at 10 call sites.

points.title: Audit and privacy
points.body: Every finance write records an audit row in the same database transaction. Payer names and account numbers are for staff only. Uploaded PDFs are checked by their magic bytes, not their extension, and served through five-minute signed URLs.

shot.caption: Uvoz izvoda · column mapping
shot.alt: Bank statement import dialog: encoding, delimiter, date and decimal format, and CSV columns mapped to fields such as poziv na broj

provisioning.title: A whole complex in one request.
provisioning.lede: The super-admin wizard and its endpoint were designed as one thing. POST /setup/bulk creates a complex, its buildings, and every unit inside one database transaction. If unit 47 fails, nothing survives, so there is no half-built complex to clean up by hand.

details: CSV import with a template that opens correctly in Serbian Excel (UTF-8 with a BOM, semicolons), a windows-1250 fallback, and row-level errors before anything is sent.
Duplicate unit numbers are caught in the form and, as a backstop, by a unique constraint per building. A request is capped at 1,000 units.
provisioning.growth: The FloorEditor replaced an earlier live tree preview, which showed the structure but couldn't edit it.

process.title: Tested against a real database.
body: The e2e suites boot the whole NestJS app and run against a real PostgreSQL database, so a passing test means the policy, the query, and the response all agree. The access matrix above is one of those suites, written as a table of actors and endpoints.

Finance carries the most tests because a mistake there costs someone money: posting and reversing entries, monthly charges that are safe to run twice, statement imports that commit all or nothing, and reports that lock their period.
Every endpoint change also lands in the Postman collection the same day, with examples, required roles, and error cases, so the API stays usable by hand as well as by tests.

designSystem.title: OKLCH, and no colour for money.
designSystem.intro: shadcn/ui over Tailwind 4's CSS-first theme. Every ramp is defined step by step in OKLCH, with a tuned dark-mode counterpart, not an inverted one, and ticket categories get their own hues: moss, rose, indigo, and plum. Finance has no colour of its own. Money uses only the status tokens, so it reads the same everywhere.

data.title: STK Vojvodina, Novi Sad
data.excerpt: STK Vojvodina is one of Serbia's most historic table tennis clubs, known for decades of competitive success and youth development in Novi Sad.
data.excerpt_xl:
STK Vojvodina is a table tennis club in Novi Sad, founded in the mid-20th century, with a record of competing at the top domestic level and a youth program that has run for decades.

The site collects club history, competition results, youth programs, and news into one structure the club can keep adding to without it falling apart.

Half the audience is a parent checking a result on a phone between matches; the rest are supporters and partners on a desktop. The site had to be fast and readable for both.
